title: Battle Engine Aquila content catalogue asset record (onslaught.content-catalog.asset.v1)
description: One line of assets.jsonl written by tools/content_catalog.py. Generated records are retail-derived metadata (names, sizes, hashes) and stay in ignored local-data/. Relationships exist only with evidence; descriptions stay null unless evidenced.

generatedRetailDerived.description: Marks generated output; tools/public_allowlist_safety_check.py refuses any tracked file carrying it.

id.description: Stable id. Files: <type>:<lower-cased install-relative path>; archive members: the container plus #chunk or #ordinal; texture records: name plus a payload-hash prefix; animations: <mesh id>/<ordinal>. Levels: level:NNN; placements: placement:<level>:<world>@<record offset>; definitions: definition:<lower-cased name>; goodies: goodie:NNN; effects: effect:<file>#<ordinal>. Markers: marker:<level>:<world>@<record offset>; waypoint paths: waypoint-path:<level>:<world>#<ordinal>; compiled scripts: script-code:<level>:<world>#<ordinal>; battle engine configurations: configuration:<file>#<record>; sound effects: sound-effect:<file>#<effect>.

name.description: The name the data stores (texture/mesh/sample name) or the file stem.

container.description: Install-relative path of the file holding the asset.

envelope.description: How the bytes are wrapped, e.g. aya-zlib-members(dds), lvlr-chunk(TEXT).

offset.description: Byte offset of the asset inside the decoded container.

chunkPath.description: Owning top-level archive chunk index (or sample ordinal). For an embedded mesh this is an anchor, not a complete PMSH/PMS2 wrapper path; offset locates the record in the inflated container.

sha256Scope.description: Which bytes sha256 covers (e.g. inflated DDS file, CMSH stream, TEXT chunk payload).

referencedBy.description: Derived reverse index: mesh ids whose resolved uses-texture links reach this record.

loadedByDescriptors.description: Derived reverse index (texture files): texture-descriptor ids whose pixels-from link resolves here.

upscale.description: Facts for HD successors and a rule-derived suggestion (textures, meshes, audio, video); null for other types. Never a visual review.

sourceResolution.description: Source dimensions. For textures these are declared by the readable DDS header; a non-null value does not admit a malformed or unsupported payload.

storedFormat.description: Format indicated by the readable DDS header. Consult texture.status for whether its payload is admitted.

sourceFormat.description: The parsed format suffix in the texture filename. The loader constructs such a suffix from a request, but the filename alone does not establish actual loading, stored DDS format or original art's bit depth.

mipLevels.description: Number of admitted mip ranges, or zero when none are admitted; declaredMipCount is the raw header field.

compressed.description: For textures, whether an admitted stored format is DXT block compressed; null when the texture is not admitted. Other asset types use their own encoding metadata.

premultipliedAlpha.description: For admitted DXT2/4 true and DXT3/5 false, the format's specified alpha association; null for DXT1, RGB, unsupported or malformed records. This is a format convention, not proof of the pixel values, actual renderer behavior or a required conversion.

tiling.description: Raw mesh UV evidence before texture transforms. The legacy repeats-beyond-0-1 status uses a 0.01 tolerance and does not establish sampler mode or visible repetition.

loader.description: The game function that reads this family (decompilation citation).

sourceFormatFromName.description: Parsed format suffix in the filename. The loader constructs such a suffix from a request, but a matching name alone does not establish loading, stored format or original art's bit depth.

storedFormat.description: Format indicated by the readable DDS header, even when status is malformed or unsupported; it is not an admission of the payload.

ddsHeader.description: Selected raw fields from the inflated DDS header. A non-null header can also occur in a malformed or unsupported texture; only status valid admits its mip byte ranges. FourCC is the four stored bytes in hex, even if its pixel-format flag is clear. Fields do not establish rendered appearance or source-art format. Older v1 records may omit this field.

mips.description: Stored levels in order; ddsOffset and sha256 refer to the encoded level bytes within the inflated DDS, not the compressed AYA or decoded pixels. Older v1 catalogs may omit index, ddsOffset and sha256.

partRecordSha256.description: SHA-256 of the 316-byte CMSP record payload.

partPayloadSha256.description: SHA-256 of the MESP part payload, without its outer chunk header.

storedBounds.description: Part's stored BBOX before hierarchy or animation transforms; not a world-space or animated bound. The flag is the stored i32, not a validation. Non-finite floats are null.

reason.description: Bounded parser refusal for an unparsed root, when present.

lodChildParts.description: Immediate child part counts; null means the child could not be parsed.

nestedMeshDetails.description: Immediate nested meshes, including unresolved or unparsed children; this is not a runtime-loading claim.

name.description: The 128-byte TEXB name field as stored: the text before the first NUL when the field is terminated and valid UTF-8 (a known-empty name is the empty string and nameStatus empty); null when the field is unterminated or not UTF-8. It is never a lossy decode of an unreadable field. A catalogue written before this field existed may hold such a decode and lacks nameStatus; it does not validate against this schema, which requires nameStatus.

nameStatus.description: utf8-decoded: a readable name. empty: the stored name is known to be empty. unterminated and invalid-utf8: the field is not a readable name, so the name is unknown, which is not the same as empty.

nameBytesSha256.description: SHA-256 of the bytes before the first NUL (the empty-input digest for an empty name); null when the field has no terminator.

requestedFormat.description: The format CMesh::FindTexture would request, from the suffix at byte 8 of a terminated, readable name longer than 8 bytes (A8 gives 4, A4 gives 2, anything else 1). null when no format is inferred: an unreadable, empty or shorter name has no suffix this catalogue classifies.

usage.description: Derived from this record's resolved relationships: placements, levels, definitions (unit/feature names), meshes, effects, goodies and code sites that use the asset. The basis for HD prioritisation; never a guess.

worlds.description: Per world body (BSWD, RLWD): header, timings, counts (CWorld::LoadWorld).

terrain.description: Decoded ERES (heightfield settings and sample summary, mixer mips, mixer map), SURF and SSHD summaries, and the mixer texture file names the map's set implies.

configurationListsAgree.description: Whether worldheaders.dat's configuration names for the level (the configuration page's list) equal its world body's header names (which the chosen slot indexes in game).

namedThings.description: Source-modelled WORLD.mNamedThings just after a successful level load (tools/named_things.py): entries in joining order (the base world's slots, then the real world's; CWorld::FindThingByName walks them from the last). A conditional entry is a base-world one, on the list only if the career keeps its slot (keep.careerBit) and its dies-on world (keep.diesOn, -1 for none) is not before the level. runtimeNames lists literal SetName calls in the level's scripts, not proof they execute. No runtime names or later changes were observed by this model.

thing.description: The placement or marker record whose init carries the name.

object.description: What joins: the record's own thing, its squad, or the member unit(s) CSquad::Init spawns (member says which, from 0).

name.description: null when the argument is not a literal.

complete.description: false when the world layout is missing or inconsistent, or a world body did not decode; undecodedWorlds names the affected parts.

placement.description: A WRES thing that names a physics definition (unit, building, squad, feature), decoded in CWorld::LoadWorld's order. slot: its index in LoadWorld's things[] (null when the physics lookup fails and the record takes none).

marker.description: Every other WRES thing (waypoint, spawner, level-script, safe-side, start, spawn-point, sphere-trigger, wingman-start, hazard, ...): its init record (CInitThing::Load and the subclass's fields).

configuration.description: A battle engine configuration modeled from Initialise and CBattleEngineData::Load (tools/game_tables_decode.py): values and stores are the effective float32 values (null when not finite). defaulted names fields supplied or overwritten by the loader. Where defaults occur, storedValues and storedStores preserve the input: a null stored float can mean absent or non-finite, and null storedStores means no store array was present. When these stored fields are omitted, the effective and stored values agree. Earlier v1 outputs may report incorrect values for versions before 8. listPosition is its place in UBattleEngineDataManager's list (each record joins the front); foundByName says whether its name finds it (a later record of the same name hides it); fallback marks the front of the list, the configuration a world header's unknown name gets.

soundEffect.description: A sound effect as CEffect::LoadSFXFile reads data/sounds/sounds.sfx (tools/game_tables_decode.py): its line, sample and low-pass sample names, volume, falloff, pitch variance and flags. chainHead is the effect the list keeps for its name (stricmp); variant is its place in that chain (0 for the head) and variants the chain's length: PlayEffect plays one of them at random.

waypointPath.description: A CWaypointPath: its member indices are slots of LoadWorld's things[]; members that are not waypoints are dropped by the loader (path-member relationships list the kept ones in order).

scriptCode.description: A compiled mission script from a world body (CWorld::LoadScripts): counts, the natives it calls and the literal arguments of those calls by role (text ids, units, waypoint paths, thing names, scripts, events).

namedThing.description: A source-modelled prediction of a named placement or marker and WORLD.mNamedThings (tools/named_things.py), assuming successful initialization: how many objects join under its name (joins, 0 when none), which (object), their entries (orders, indexes into the level's namedThings.entries), whether its own name finds it immediately after loading (foundByName) and, for a base-world record, the career's condition (keep). It is not an observation of runtime names or changes.

registryIncomplete.description: World parts missing, inconsistent or undecoded; the partial registry cannot establish the name lookup.

reason.description: Why nothing joins: the record took no slot, it is a tree or waypoint (CThing), or its unit is UB_JEEP (SpawnThing makes nothing).

diesOn.description: The dies_on[] value at the slot when the start loop reads it: the record's own dies-on world, or what the last record that failed to take the slot wrote (-1 for none).

kind.description: loader-code: a function in the public decompilation decides the link; data: the bytes themselves state it.

target.description: An id of a record in the same catalogue (never an absent id), or null when unresolved or several targets apply (then targets lists them).

status.description: unknown-name: the mesh slot's stored name field is unreadable (unterminated or not UTF-8), so nothing was looked up or joined; empty-name: the slot's stored name is known to be empty and nothing was joined; both differ from unresolved, where a readable name matched nothing: it was looked up and found nothing or, for a name shorter than 9 bytes that has no suffix from byte 8 to classify, nothing was looked up or joined (the evidence says which). name-match: a stored string equals a file name but no loader joins them; name-match-unloaded: a data observation about content no retail loader reads; code-site: a literal lookup in game code (the evidence names the site); code-rule: a name game code builds with sprintf from a format rule and data (the evidence names the function and the rule). name-match also covers a script argument that equals a thing's name. For names-thing (a source-modelled lookup of a script's literal name just after a successful load): resolved predicts the target in every career (shadowed lists records of the same name it hides); career-dependent predicts that every matching record is in the base world, so the first one the career keeps is found (candidates lists them in that order, target is the first); runtime-name predicts no match immediately after load but a script contains a literal SetName call that could assign it if executed (setBy names the scripts); unresolved predicts no match; incomplete means a missing, inconsistent or undecoded world part prevents a reliable prediction. These are not runtime observations.

targetNameStatus.description: For uses-texture: the stored-name status of the mesh slot, as in mesh.textures[].nameStatus.

candidates.description: For names-thing (career-dependent): the records of the name in the order FindThingByName meets them. For incomplete names-thing, candidates are only the matches visible in the partial model. For incomplete plays-sample, candidates contain matching records from standard language banks where a bank has duplicate names; actual load success and selection are unobserved. Neither incomplete case establishes the actual target.

shadowed.description: For names-thing (resolved): records of the same name that joined earlier, found only after the target leaves the list.

via.description: For names-thing on a cutscene marker: the name is its link-to name, which CCutscene::Start looks up when the cutscene starts (a script's names-thing has natives instead).

fallback.description: For offers-configuration from a world header: the configuration GetConfiguration(0) gives when the name matches nothing.

registryIncomplete.description: For names-thing: world parts missing, inconsistent or undecoded, so the partial list cannot establish the answer.

setBy.description: For names-thing (runtime-name): the script-code records whose SetName call gives the name, and the call's instruction index.
